title: Beyond Benchmark Performance in Ophthalmic AI: A Review and Evidence Gap Map
shortTitle: Beyond Benchmark Performance in Ophthalmic AI
abstract: Ophthalmology combines detailed imaging with longitudinal measurements that inform screening, monitoring, and treatment, providing a distinctive setting for clinical artificial intelligence (AI). We reviewed 427 English-language publications involving optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography (OCTA), or related ophthalmic imaging, identified from 6,482 harmonised records retrieved from PubMed, ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus through April 2026. Applications extended beyond image classification to multimodal interpretation, prediction of disease course and treatment need, and clinical workflow support. Evidence mapping showed extensive attention to model performance but substantially less to implementation and its consequences, with further gaps in economic evaluation, regulation, cybersecurity, privacy, and accountability. Evidence in these domains provides a foundation for the next stage of clinical translation. Progress can build on this foundation through representative external validation, interoperable data, effective human oversight, and prospective evaluation of safety, equity, and patient and service outcomes. Evaluating ophthalmic AI across the care pathway is therefore essential to establish whether model outputs improve clinical decisions and deliver measurable benefits for patients and health services.
status: Review manuscript prepared for The Lancet Digital Health

progression: Prediction of disease course or treatment need
scopeStatement: All included publications addressed ophthalmic imaging data. The evidence map is distinct from contextual references in the bibliography.
evidenceMapCaution: The evidence-gap maps summarise how publications frame each dimension. They do not represent pooled effect sizes, diagnostic-accuracy estimates, risk-of-bias ratings, or certainty-of-evidence assessments.
